resolution: Contrast 45bb643335247013ac2e77e5 (root-only DRY_BIOMASS, E1.SB.ROOT vs E1.S, 30 d) was checked against the rendered original PDF p7, Table 1, column 'Root dry weight (g)', block 'Saline conditions'. Row 'Root dipping' prints 0.29 +/- 0.033 (letter a); row 'Positive control' prints 0.05 +/- 0.007 (letter b). Stored mean_t, sd_t, mean_c and sd_c match these cells exactly, and ln(0.29/0.05)=1.758 and the stored variance reproduce from them with n=3. The caption states mean +/- SD with n=3 replicates per treatment. Methods on p11 (receipt SRC-3d4e758fb7526a059ea99207) confirm the basis: roots and shoots oven dried separately at 60 C for 3 days, and uninoculated saline plants are the positive control. The unit is printed as bare g with one plant per pot. No transcription, unit, arm or basis error was found, so this is a source-supported large effect driven by a very small control mean: the same 0.05 denominator gives larger ratios for the other three inoculated saline rows (0.44, 0.50, 0.72). The control mean is printed to two decimals only, so rounding alone allows lnRR of about 1.66 to 1.86. The value is retained, not deleted or winsorized. Limitations stay flagged: (1) Methods p11 say each treatment was replicated five times while the Table 1 caption says n=3. This conflict affects the variance, not the lnRR. (2) Table 1 has a source anomaly: the Normal-block inoculated shoot cells duplicate the Saline-block root cells of the same rows, including 0.29 +/- 0.033 under Normal/Root dipping/Shoot dry weight. The Saline root cells carry significance letters and the Normal copies do not, and the copied Normal shoot lengths (for example 7.7 cm against 24.8 cm in the negative control) are implausible, so the Normal shoot cells are the more likely misprint. This is an inference from the printed table, not a statement by the authors, and the source does not definitively exclude an error in the Saline root column. Fruit yield is not involved: this is a 30-d root dry-weight outcome.

Arithmetic was done by hand. Printed means match the packet measurements ARM05 mean 3.2 and ARM02 mean 0.49 in g/plant, so there is no transcription error. Results prose on physical p.5 (receipt SRC-ebc76e410eacaafbf17148e4, PNG read) repeats 0.49 g/plant as the lowest LDW mean, under 250 mM NaCl, so the source is consistent on the denominator, although that prose may derive from the same table. Design from physical p.3 Section 2.2 and p.4 Section 2.3.4 (receipts SRC-3adaf430ee04706dd170957c, SRC-81cfbb600a67167f92813f12): completely randomized design, four replications, pot as experimental unit with three plants per pot, so n=4 pots. ROW-11 IDENTITY: the table prints '100/250' twice, but row 11 is mapped to 200 mM NaCl + 250 mg/L L-GLU on source evidence: Methods 2.1.1 lists group 11 as 200NaCl-250GLU and the table rows follow the Methods order 1-12 (p.3, receipt SRC-2187437a074ac11b987d5620); the Figure 1 axes print the corresponding position as '200/250' (p.7, receipt SRC-2b1a9269418d399c4ffe8928); the p.5 prose on reduced shoot height names 100NaCl-250GLU, 100NaCl-500GLU and 200NaCl-250GLU, matching Table 3 rows 9-11 (15.96, 14.76, 17.92 vs control 20.33); the p.6 prose on reduced chlorophyll names the same three groups, matching Table 5 rows 9-11 chlorophyll a (0.184, 0.293, 0.308 vs control 0.381) (receipt SRC-27053d698eb0d396750c04a4). The mapping is a source-supported inference: the paper prints no erratum for the row label, and the label conflict stays recorded on E2.S200B250. Legacy arm 651_AMB_ROW11 notes still say to exclude this row until the label is confirmed; that legacy note is superseded in the current design only by the mapping above and is not independently changed here. LIMITATIONS KEPT WITH THE FLAG: 'Fruit FW' prints no unit; ± type is not stated (SE only under the project assumption, never author-reported); footnote '±: n=3' conflicts with Methods 2.1.2 '10 randomly selected fruits' and with 9 pots/3 replications per group, so independent n is unconfirmed; the abstract lists 200NaCl among the lowest morphological values while Table 4 shows it with the highest-letter fruit FW, and the table value is retained over prose. No biological explanation for the 200 mM NaCl increase in mean fruit mass is given by the source and none is asserted. SCOPE: endpoint is MEAN_FRUIT_MASS, individual fruit fresh weight from 10 sampled fruits, a supporting productivity measure and not a substitute for fruit-yield mass; this decision does not create or alter any fruit-yield record.

message: MEAN_FRUIT_MASS lnRR=-0.644 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=4.7 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: Rule C001 WARN on an_contrasts c53b84a6952acb7389ebbc31, MEAN_FRUIT_MASS lnRR=-0.644. Read in the rendered original PDF page 5 (printed p. 331, receipt SRC-7cd17badce00a4ed246329e7), Table 4, column 'Fruit FW': row 'NaCl mM 200' = 75.4±10.91a; row 'NaCl/L-GLU 200/500' = 39.6±9.64e. ln(39.6/75.4) = -0.644. Contrast identity is INFERRED, because the packet gives only the contrast id and the arms were not read from an_contrasts: among the 12 printed Fruit FW means (36.8, 41.8, 53.4, 75.4, 61.6, 53.8, 33.6, 76.8, 57.6, 32.0, 34.4, 39.6) 39.6 over 75.4 is the only ordered pair that rounds to -0.644, which corresponds to 200 mM NaCl + 500 mg/L L-GLU versus 200 mM NaCl alone. Both means are exact printed values and match packet records for this table; no transcription, unit or arm error was found for these two cells. The reduction is also supported by the source's own significance letters (a versus e), and the 200 mM value is the source's high value rather than an extraction artefact. The |z_MAD|=4.7 statistic was taken from the issue message and not recomputed. This is a true source value: retain with the flag, with no deletion or winsorizing. Limitations to keep attached: the Fruit FW header prints no unit, and packet unit is 'source unit'. The ± type is not stated, so SE remains a project assumption and is not author-reported. The table footnote '(±: n=3)' conflicts with Methods 2.1.2 '10 randomly selected fruits', and Methods 2.1.1 reports 9 pots with 3 replications per group (page 3, printed p. 329, receipt SRC-949154e31221d1e96a70029d), so inferential n is unresolved. Scope: Fruit FW from 10 selected fruits is treated as mean individual fruit mass, a separate endpoint and not harvested fruit yield; the flag therefore does not touch the primary yield target. Both cells are outside the duplicated row-11 '100/250' label ambiguity.

message: MEAN_FRUIT_MASS lnRR=1.154 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=5.7 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: True source-supported outlier; retain with flag, no deletion, winsorizing or value change. Original PDF physical page 10 (printed p.131), Table (9) 'weight of one fruit (g)', read in the PNG at 180 dpi (this receipt) and 300 dpi (SRC-7898efec837b66ce20137ecd): 2021 column H1, row CK = '26.22 c'; row P3 = '83.15 a'. ln(83.15/26.22)=1.154 reproduces the flagged lnRR. The an_contrasts row itself is not in the packet, so the pair is identified by this arithmetic; no other within-hybrid/year treatment-vs-CK pair in Table 9 gives 1.154 (the others span about 0.60 to 0.92). The stored measurements (2021_H1_CK 26.22 g and 2021_H1_P3 83.15 g, n=3) match the printed cells. Checks that this is not a transcription or scale error: (1) the page 10 prose independently prints H1 treated with P3 as 83.15 g in the first season; (2) the printed Mean (Treatments) reproduce from the cells, (83.15+23.97)/2=53.56 and (26.22+11.93)/2=19.08 (rounded); (3) Table 8 marketable weight divided by Table 6 marketable number (physical page 9, receipt SRC-b075923103b16e90ed75a26f) gives 15.80 ton feddan-1 / 190133 = 83.10 g for P3 and 3.48 ton feddan-1 / 133200 = 26.13 g for CK, consistent with both cells to within rounding; these tables are probably not independent measurements, so this confirms internal consistency, not accuracy; (4) Duncan letters separate P3 (a) from CK (c) with LSD A*B 5.75. Scientific context: the magnitude reflects a low CK and the highest P3 cell in 2021; the same contrast in 2022 is 39.68 versus 19.46 g (lnRR 0.713), so the size of the effect varies by season and the retained flag should stay visible in analyses. Means are of three replicates per the Table 9 footnote; no SD/SE is printed, so no variance is available from this table. Known limitation left unchanged: the printed 2021 H2 Mean (Hybrids) 58.98 a does not match its cells (mean 20.14), but that marginal is excluded and does not enter this contrast. MEAN_FRUIT_MASS is not a fruit-yield substitute, and this decision changes no FRUIT_YIELD record.

message: MEAN_FRUIT_MASS lnRR=0.976 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=4.7 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: True outlier in the source; retain unchanged, no deletion or winsorizing. CONTRAST: an_contrasts 3737c8892f0ff8fbd64d0088 is E2.SB40 (Irrig60xSe40xSA, EXP01_ARM12) vs E2.S (Irrig60xSe0xSA, EXP01_ARM08), season 2017, T90DAT, MEAN_FRUIT_MASS, stored means 138.151 and 52.042 g, lnRR 0.9763. ORIGINAL FIGURE (PDF p13, Fig. 9 top panel, black 2017 series, receipt SRC-a05865a90eb22e6b6ffa771d, 600 dpi): my own gridded reading against the 0-250 g axis (six ticks, about 165 px per 50 g) gives about 137.9 and 51.6 g, lnRR about 0.98. This is a check reading to about +-0.5 g, not a replacement digitization. The compact letters also separate the arms (f vs bc). AUTHORS' PROSE (PDF p12, section 3.6, receipt SRC-b7afe1a7026a4a7367031b82; control named at top of p13): Irrig60xSe40xSA 'significantly increased average fruit weight by 164.6 and 109.9 %' vs Irrig60xSe0xSA. 164.6 % implies lnRR 0.973; stored pct_effect is 165.46 %, a ratio difference of about 0.3 %. The first value matches 2017. TABLE 10 CROSS-CHECK (PDF p13, printed marginal means, 2017): the 12 stored 2017 arm means reproduce them: 100 % WHC 158.87 vs 159.1; 60 % WHC 90.85 vs 91.2; Se0 99.34 vs 99.9; Se40 152.71 vs 152.7; foliar 122.99 vs 123.4; soil 126.73 vs 126.9. All are within 0.6 %. This supports the arm means and arm assignment; marginal means were used only as a check, never as cells. COMPONENT CROSS-CHECK (stored Fig. 9 values, 2017): fruit number x mean fruit mass approximates fruit yield per plant: E2.S 7.052 x 52.042 g = 0.367 kg vs 0.371 kg; E2.SB40 25.93 x 138.151 g = 3.582 kg vs 3.599 kg. INTERPRETATION: the extreme lnRR comes from a very low severe-deficit control (about 52 g, vs about 145 g in the well-watered Se0 arms) and a strong recovery with soil-applied Se. Fruit mass is measured per plant at 90 DAT (Methods 2.3/2.4, PDF p2-3, receipts SRC-5d4de0c2670a81e30d7c5711 and SRC-f60f5b795611c523be65696a). No unit, arm, series or transcription error was found. The Irrig60 Se0 arm is the authors' own named control. MEAN_FRUIT_MASS is a yield component, not a fruit-yield substitute. NOTES, none of which changes this decision: (1) This contrast has no variance (sd and n null; flag DEPENDENT_OR_UNKNOWN_ALLOCATION_VARIANCE_UNAVAILABLE). The original states 'Split-Split design' (PDF p2, receipt SRC-5d4de0c2670a81e30d7c5711) and 'factorial completely randomized design' with 15 replications (pots) and mean +- SE (section 2.11, PDF p4, receipt SRC-5427de57d41ecceaacda1e29), and does not state n for fruit traits in the pages read here (p2-4, p12-13). (2) All 24 records each of MEAN_FRUIT_MASS, FRUIT_NUMBER and DRY_BIOMASS store dispersion_type_reported=OTHER_INTERVAL, while all 24 FRUIT_YIELD records store SE. Section 2.11 states mean +- SE for the data generally, so the OTHER_INTERVAL label looks inconsistent and should be checked. This is a metadata query only; I did not change it. (3) All 24 FRUIT_YIELD records have sd null and dispersion_type UNCLEAR: 12 of 2017 and 5 of 2018 are NOT_READABLE, and 7 of 2018 are DIGITIZED_UPPER_ONLY. Caps are visibly printed in Fig. 9. I did not retest whether they meet the 5 % limit, so I make no claim that these statuses are wrong. PROCESS: a direct read-only Python query of the database was blocked by the project guard; I then used the approved 'tfm.py sql' SELECT command. I added one helper crop, T-006424_fig9_top.png, in the receipt folder work/source_views/SRC-a05865a90eb22e6b6ffa771d/; the receipt's recorded assets are unchanged.

message: MEAN_FRUIT_MASS lnRR=1.427 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=7.3 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: True source-supported outlier; retain with flag, no deletion or winsorizing. Original PDF p5, Figure 6 (y-axis 'Average fruit weight/plant', 0-90, ticks every 10, caption 'Error bars indicate +/-SD'), Elisabeta group, after third treatment: AT x 120 mM NaCl bar reads about 62 (SD cap about 70, letter a); 120 mM NaCl bar reads about 15 (SD cap about 18, letter bc). ln(62.4/15) = about 1.43, matching flagged lnRR=1.427 (ratio 4.17). The other three cultivars give about 0.47 (Buzau 33.5/21), -0.15 (Bacovia 25.5/29.5) and 0.38 (Lillagro 39.5/27), so only Elisabeta fits. Attribution of contrast 1faf9d703f6035685fe042bd to Elisabeta is by this arithmetic and the issue message; the contrast row itself was not opened. The size arises from the very low S denominator, visible in the figure and not a misread axis or swapped legend: the source's own Tukey letters separate the two bars, the Elisabeta NaCl bar is the lowest in the panel, and prose on the same page says 120 mM values were much lower than control. Figure 5 on the same page shows the same direction (Elisabeta about 11 fruits with Atonik plus NaCl versus about 3 with NaCl alone). Readings were visual on the 200 dpi (SRC-83a80e0d097e5d708fefe701) and 400 dpi renders, a check of the flag and not a new calibrated digitization. Limitations that remain: Figure 6 prints no unit and its label is ambiguous between mean individual fruit mass and per-plant mass; p9 (SRC-164e1d26742dd3b03b7a339c) describes design and treatments with no harvest event in the part read; p11 (SRC-6663443e9abf09d723090b30) is conclusions and references, not relevant. This contrast is MEAN_FRUIT_MASS, a non-substitute for fruit yield; this decision does not reclassify Figure 6 or change slot #03, which remains NOT_EXTRACTABLE, and it adds no fruit-yield value.

DRY_BIOMASS lnRR=2.667 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=7.9 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: Contrast 95b2024aab3c33261e651c35 (SB_vs_S, root-only DRY_BIOMASS, E1.H30, E1.SB.SEED_SOIL vs E1.S; read with tfm.py sql). Original PDF p.7 Table 1 rendered at 250 dpi and read as an image, block 'Saline conditions', column 'Root dry weight (g)': row 'Seed treatment + soil drenching' prints 0.72 +/- 0.046 (letter d); row 'Positive control' prints 0.05 +/- 0.007 (letter b). The stored mean_t 0.72, sd_t 0.046, mean_c 0.05, sd_c 0.007 match these cells, and lnRR = ln(0.72/0.05) = 2.667 is arithmetically correct. Unit and basis: printed g, with Methods p.11 (receipt SRC-8721a705d484aade2da7117d) stating that roots and shoots were oven dried at 60 C for 3 days to constant weight, one plant per pot, harvest after 30 days. The size of the effect comes from a very small shared saline control (0.05 g, against 0.23 g in the normal negative control). It is in line with the sibling root contrasts against the same control (0.44/0.05, 0.29/0.05, 0.50/0.05, lnRR about 2.18, 1.76, 2.30) and with the shoot contrast for the same arm (2.80/0.23, lnRR about 2.50). No transcription, unit or arm error was found, so the outlier is retained unchanged, flagged, not deleted or winsorized. Limitations carried with the flag: (1) The control mean is printed to one significant figure; rounding alone (0.045-0.055) spans lnRR about 2.57-2.77. (2) Table 1 caption and Statistics give n=3, while Methods p.11 says each treatment was replicated five times; the contrast uses the caption n=3, and this conflict affects var_effect, not the point effect. (3) Source integrity caveat, not resolved by this decision: on p.7 the 12 saline-block root cells for the four inoculated rows are identical to the normal-block shoot cells of the same rows, including this numerator (0.72 +/- 0.046 also appears as normal seed treatment + soil drenching Shoot dry Weight). Internal evidence favours the saline root cells being the originals and the normal shoot cells being the misplaced copies: only the saline block carries letters; saline root values sit just below the normal root values for each route (0.44 vs 0.49, 0.29 vs 0.31, 0.50 vs 0.57, 0.72 vs 0.88 g); and the normal shoot copies would put inoculated non-saline shoots far below both the normal control and the same routes under salt, contradicting the text. This is inference, not proof: no original source prints the values independently. Discussion p.9 (receipt SRC-2832bea2dc72f2f65b1d38ae) supports only the direction of the effect, stating that seed + soil drench gave the highest root/shoot dry weight, and the supplement holds only bacterial characterization tables by keyword search of its parsed text, so neither corroborates the number. The packet already marks the normal-block shoot fresh and dry cells AMBIGUOUS. The contrast's DOUBLE_AGREE status shows agreement on transcription, not that the printed cell is correct. Study fruit yield is ABSENT in triage (30-day harvest, no fruit stage), so this contrast does not touch fruit-yield data.

message: DRY_BIOMASS lnRR=2.499 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=7.3 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: Retain as a source-supported outlier; no value deleted, winsorized or changed. Original PDF p7 Table 1 (rendered PNG read), section 'Saline conditions', column 'Shoot dry Weight (g)': row 'Positive control' 0.23 ± 0.001 (b); row 'Seed treatment + soil drenching' 2.80 ± 0.018 (e). These match the stored records 279_EXP01_ARM06 (mean 0.23, SD 0.001) and 279_EXP01_ARM10 (mean 2.8, SD 0.018). ln(2.80/0.23)=2.499, equal to the flagged lnRR, so the outlier comes from printed values, not from a transcription or unit error. Limitation: the packet does not include the an_contrasts row for entity 284911f541a18d64268e3ebe, so this pairing is inferred arithmetically. It is the only same-organ saline dry-weight pair in Table 1 that gives 2.499 (root 0.72/0.05 gives 2.667; shoot+root sum (2.80+0.72)/(0.23+0.05) gives 2.531). Basis and timing: PDF p11 (receipt SRC-8721a705d484aade2da7117d) states roots and shoots were oven dried separately at 60 °C for 3 days to constant weight after 30 days of inoculation and salt exposure; the Table 1 caption also gives harvest after 30 days. Unit is bare g, and the design thins to one seedling per pot. Caveats to keep with the flag: (1) Replication conflict: Table 1 caption says n=3 replicates per treatment, while p11 says each treatment was replicated five times; the record uses n=3. (2) The control SD of 0.001 on 0.23 is unusually small, so inverse-variance weight for this contrast would be inflated. (3) The fold change in shoot dry weight (12.2) far exceeds that in shoot fresh weight (15.78/4.56=3.5 from the same rows), with implied dry/fresh ratios of 5.0% versus 17.7%; the paper does not explain this, so it cannot be called a typesetting error. (4) The known suspected duplication in Table 1 affects normal-condition inoculated shoot cells, which repeat saline root cells; the saline shoot dry weight column used here is not part of that duplicated block. This issue concerns a 30-day vegetative dry-biomass endpoint and does not affect fruit-yield data.

message: DRY_BIOMASS lnRR=2.132 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=6.1 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: Contrast identity: the an_contrasts row ee20ff99d30e0bbdd78c0299 is not in the packet, so its arms were identified by arithmetic, not read from the row. lnRR=2.132 is reproduced only by ln(1.94/0.23)=2.1324 among the saline-arm dry-weight pairs (others: 0.44/0.05=2.175, 0.50/0.05=2.303, 0.72/0.05=2.667, 0.29/0.05=1.758, 1.85/0.23=2.085, 0.58/0.23=0.925, 2.80/0.23=2.499). That is saline soil drenching (279_EXP01_ARM09, 279_M0056) versus saline positive control (279_EXP01_ARM06, 279_M0038), shoot dry weight at the 30-day harvest. Source check: original PDF physical p7 Table 1, read in the PNG, column 'Shoot dry Weight (g)', section 'Saline conditions': row 'Soil drenching' prints 1.94 +/- 0.058 (letter c), row 'Positive control' prints 0.23 +/- 0.001 (letter b). Both match the database means and SDs, so this is not a transcription, row or column error. Unit is g in both cells, same experiment and timepoint. Dry basis confirmed on p11 (receipt SRC-8721a705d484aade2da7117d): roots and shoots oven dried at 60 C for 3 days till constant weight. Not affected by the known Table 1 duplication: normal-condition inoculated shoot length/fresh/dry cells duplicate saline root length/fresh/dry cells, but the saline shoot dry column is outside that block. The effect is large but printed and directionally consistent with Table 1 (saline inoculated arms exceed the saline control in shoot dry weight) and with the Fig. 5 photograph on p6 (receipt SRC-f19f424d76176795cbdbb6e3). No original source value supports correcting it; retain unchanged, no deletion or winsorizing. Caveats kept with the flag: (1) the dry ratio 8.43 far exceeds the fresh ratio 13.43/4.56=2.95 in the same rows, implying dry matter fractions of 14.4% versus 5.0%; across saline inoculated arms the fraction varies from 5.7% (root dipping) to 21.1% (seed treatment). This is a plausibility concern about the source, not evidence of a specific misprint. (2) The control SD of 0.001 is unusually small and inflates precision if the contrast is weighted. (3) Replication conflict: the Table 1 caption says n=3 and p12 Statistics says triplicates (receipt SRC-1346fb61d6db7872855cb338), while p11 Methods says each treatment was replicated five times in a completely randomized block design. The recorded n=3 follows the table caption; lnRR is unaffected, variance depends on it. (4) ARM06 is a shared control across saline contrasts and must stay in its dependency cluster. Supplement checked (receipt SRC-81f2fa2d13bdf083f4d742a0, text search of the original view, not a visual review): it holds Fig. S1 and Tables S1-S3 on bacterial characterization, with no matches for dry weight, biomass or shoot, so it offers no competing value. Scope: this study harvested plants at 30 d and reports no fruit-yield values in the pages reviewed here; this decision concerns DRY_BIOMASS only and is not a fruit-yield absence review.

message: DRY_BIOMASS lnRR=1.736 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=4.8 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: True outlier retained; no value deleted, corrected or winsorized. CONTRAST: an_contrasts row e867923c4afc04d43d1716ad, read directly: SB_vs_S, leaf scope, g/plant, arm_key_t E1.SB.BPUM.ZnO20 mean 2.78, arm_key_c E1.S mean 0.49, n 4 and 4, effect 1.7358. SOURCE: original PDF physical p.6, Table 2, LDW (g/plant) column (receipt SRC-9375d21a107cfac47ac7ea14, PNG read at 220 dpi): row 'Salinity stress + Bacillus pumilus + 20 mg L-1 ZnO-NPs' prints 2.78 +/- 1.2 bc; row '250 mM NaCl' prints 0.49 +/- 0.9 f. The record means match the printed cells and ln(2.78/0.49) reproduces the flagged 1.736, so there is no transcription, arm or unit error. Results prose on physical p.5 (receipt SRC-ebc76e410eacaafbf17148e4, PNG read) repeats 0.49 g/plant as the lowest LDW mean, under 250 mM NaCl; this may derive from the same table, so it is consistency, not independent confirmation. CORROBORATION OF SIZE, same two rows on p.6, hand arithmetic: LFW 18.43/3.19 gives lnRR about 1.754; RFW 2.17/0.41 gives about 1.666; RDW 0.21/0.08 gives about 0.965; LDW/LFW is about 0.151 treated and 0.154 NaCl. The large effect reflects a strong reported response from a very low stressed baseline. This shows internal consistency only; it cannot prove the authors' data correct. DESIGN: p.3 Section 2.2 (receipt SRC-3adaf430ee04706dd170957c) states factorial, completely randomized, four replications; p.4 Section 2.3.4 (receipt SRC-81cfbb600a67167f92813f12) states each pot is the experimental unit with three plants selected per pot, Duncan's test; n=4 pots supported. Both arms share cultivar Linda and the experiment. LIMITATIONS THAT STAY WITH THE FLAG: (1) VARIANCE OF THIS CONTRAST IS NOT CREDIBLE AS STORED. The printed +/- is unlabelled; pages 3-6 read here define no SD or SE, so USER_ASSUMED_SE applies and the record has sd_c=1.8 and var_effect 3.5599, almost entirely from the comparator ((0.9/0.49)^2 about 3.37). For four non-negative pot values with mean 0.49, the largest possible SE equals the mean (0.49) and the largest possible SD is 0.98, so 0.9 cannot be an SE at n=4 and SD 1.8 is arithmetically impossible. Read as an SD, 0.9 would be barely possible. A misprint is plausible but the true value is not established; no replacement such as 0.09 is proposed or applied, and the printed 0.9 is preserved. This also makes effect_bc=0.142 unreliable as a correction, since it is driven by the same term. Weighted use of this contrast is unsafe, and exclusion via weighted_reported_uncertainty_only_eligible or an unweighted sensitivity analysis is advised; the same concern sits in open P003 issue 11391 and V009 issue 4899 (CV=3.67), which this decision does not close. The lnRR point value does not depend on the +/-, which is why this C001 flag is retained rather than escalated. The same pattern affects other Table 2 cells (RDW 0.21 +/- 0.81, 0.27 +/- 0.80, 0.31 +/- 0.7). (2) Comparator 0.49 is shared across SB_vs_S contrasts in this study (shared_control_id recorded; dependency cluster DC-D_0783aeacf190137b). (3) Leaf-only dry mass in seedlings, not whole-plant terminal biomass; sampling day is not stated, and Section 2.2 says only that fresh leaves were collected prior to flowering. (4) Methods name leaf dry weight and precision scales but state no oven or drying procedure; the header and Methods do say dry weight. (5) The treated arm is a PGPB plus ZnO-NP combination, and Table 2 publishes no no-bacteria plus ZnO row, so the effect cannot be attributed to one component. FRUIT YIELD: this flag concerns DRY_BIOMASS only and Table 2 has no fruit-yield column, so no retained fruit-yield data are affected. Only physical pp.3-6 were read for this issue; this is not a study-wide fruit-yield absence review.

resolution: True source-supported outlier; retain, no deletion or winsorizing. Contrast 025d17933de16d83f3f4dee9 (SB_vs_S, leaf dry weight, g/plant). message: DRY_BIOMASS lnRR=1.952 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=5.5 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: Genuine source-supported large effect; retain without deletion or winsorizing. Contrast identity: the an_contrasts row 0221ef7825d9eeec57cf0f0f was not exposed in the packet or by the contrasts CLI (counts only: 18 SB_vs_S, 2 S_vs_C), so it was identified arithmetically. Recomputing all 20 from the original Table 2 means, the only match to lnRR=1.952 is LDW (leaf dry weight, g/plant), Salinity stress + Lactobacillus casei + 40 mg/L ZnO-NPs (ARM08) 3.45 vs 250 mM NaCl (ARM02) 0.49: ln(3.45/0.49)=1.952. Next closest is L. casei + 20 mg/L at 1.892. Source check, PDF p.6 Table 2, read on rendered PNG (receipt above): row '250 mM NaCl', column LDW prints '0.49 ± 0.9 f'; row 'Salinity stress + Lactobacillus casei + 40 mg L-1 ZnO-NPs', column LDW prints '3.45 ± 0.9 a'. Stored means and dispersions match the print, so this is not a transcription error. Independent confirmation in the same original, PDF p.5 Section 3.1 (receipt SRC-ebc76e410eacaafbf17148e4): the prose names L. casei + 40 as the highest LDW at 3.45 g/plant and 250 mM NaCl stress as the lowest at 0.49 g/plant. Duncan letters a vs f also separate them, and the F value is significant at p<=0.01. Why it is extreme: it pairs the study's highest and lowest LDW, and the ratio of about 7 is consistent in direction with LFW in the same rows (24.67 vs 3.19). Limitations, kept as flags and not corrected: (1) The printed ±0.9 on a mean of 0.49 g/plant exceeds the mean and sits oddly with letter f; a misprint of 0.09 is possible but unproven, so no correction is proposed and the printed value stands, making any variance for this contrast very wide. (2) PDF p.4 Section 2.3.4 (receipt SRC-81cfbb600a67167f92813f12) and Table 2 footnotes do not define ±, so SE is the USER_ASSUMED_SE project assumption, not an author report, despite stored stat_basis 'mean ± SE'. (3) PDF p.3 Section 2.2 (receipt SRC-3adaf430ee04706dd170957c) labels LDW 'leaf dry weight' measured with precision scales and gives no oven or drying procedure on pp.3-4; dry-basis rests on the label, relevant to strict-mart eligibility under author decision 6. (4) This is leaf-only, a partial shoot fallback at a pre-flowering seedling sampling, and the numerator is a combined PGPB + ZnO-NP arm. n=4 pots with pot as experimental unit (p.3 'four replications', p.4). No fruit-yield data are involved in this issue; yield_status in the packet is ABSENT.

message: DRY_BIOMASS lnRR=2.234 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=6.4 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: True outlier, retained unchanged. Original PDF p9 Table 2, column DW (g), read on the rendered PNG: salt 7 g/L Untreated 0.03 +/- 0.01; salt 7 g/L FMH45 0.28 +/- 0.13**. ln(0.28/0.03)=2.2336, matching the flagged lnRR=2.234, so the extraction carries the printed cells without transcription or unit error (both cells in g, same column). Contrast identification is arithmetic: the an_contrasts row a6a230cfff8440d62f85a1fb itself was not read, because the guard limits agents to approved CLI commands; the same ratio would also arise from 7 g/L FMH45 against 10 g/L Untreated (0.03), which is not a same-salinity inoculation contrast. Cause of extremity: a very small denominator printed to one significant figure after near-total growth failure of untreated plants. Print rounding alone gives lnRR about 2.06 to 2.43, so the flag is not a rounding artefact. Corroboration in the original: Table 2 FW at 7 g/L is 0.3 +/- 0.1 vs 2.8 +/- 1.4**, the same ratio; FW x (1 - WC/100) with WC 90 gives 0.28 for FMH45, and with WC 87 gives about 0.04 for Untreated, compatible with printed rounding; two-way ANOVA treatment x salinity for DW P=0.011 (Table 2). Receipt SRC-7d7587d675e3a88783c10c7d p8 Fig. 2a photographs show strongly reduced untreated plants vs leafy FMH45 plants at 7 g/L, and Fig. 2b shows plant elongation and leaf number at 7 g/L far higher with FMH45. resolution: Contrast 45bb643335247013ac2e77e5 (root-only DRY_BIOMASS, E1.SB.ROOT vs E1.S, 30 d) was checked against the rendered original PDF p7, Table 1, column 'Root dry weight (g)', block 'Saline conditions'. Row 'Root dipping' prints 0.29 +/- 0.033 (letter a); row 'Positive control' prints 0.05 +/- 0.007 (letter b). Stored mean_t, sd_t, mean_c and sd_c match these cells exactly, and ln(0.29/0.05)=1.758 and the stored variance reproduce from them with n=3. The caption states mean +/- SD with n=3 replicates per treatment. Methods on p11 (receipt SRC-3d4e758fb7526a059ea99207) confirm the basis: roots and shoots oven dried separately at 60 C for 3 days, and uninoculated saline plants are the positive control. The unit is printed as bare g with one plant per pot. No transcription, unit, arm or basis error was found, so this is a source-supported large effect driven by a very small control mean: the same 0.05 denominator gives larger ratios for the other three inoculated saline rows (0.44, 0.50, 0.72). The control mean is printed to two decimals only, so rounding alone allows lnRR of about 1.66 to 1.86. The value is retained, not deleted or winsorized. Limitations stay flagged: (1) Methods p11 say each treatment was replicated five times while the Table 1 caption says n=3. This conflict affects the variance, not the lnRR. (2) Table 1 has a source anomaly: the Normal-block inoculated shoot cells duplicate the Saline-block root cells of the same rows, including 0.29 +/- 0.033 under Normal/Root dipping/Shoot dry weight. The Saline root cells carry significance letters and the Normal copies do not, and the copied Normal shoot lengths (for example 7.7 cm against 24.8 cm in the negative control) are implausible, so the Normal shoot cells are the more likely misprint. This is an inference from the printed table, not a statement by the authors, and the source does not definitively exclude an error in the Saline root column. The stored mean_t 0.72, sd_t 0.046, mean_c 0.05, sd_c 0.007 match these cells, and lnRR = ln(0.72/0.05) = 2.667 is arithmetically correct. Unit and basis: printed g, with Methods p.11 (receipt SRC-8721a705d484aade2da7117d) stating that roots and shoots were oven dried at 60 C for 3 days to constant weight, one plant per pot, harvest after 30 days. The size of the effect comes from a very small shared saline control (0.05 g, against 0.23 g in the normal negative control). It is in line with the sibling root contrasts against the same control (0.44/0.05, 0.29/0.05, 0.50/0.05, lnRR about 2.18, 1.76, 2.30) and with the shoot contrast for the same arm (2.80/0.23, lnRR about 2.50). (2) Table 1 caption and Statistics give n=3, while Methods p.11 says each treatment was replicated five times; the contrast uses the caption n=3, and this conflict affects var_effect, not the point effect. (3) Source integrity caveat, not resolved by this decision: on p.7 the 12 saline-block root cells for the four inoculated rows are identical to the normal-block shoot cells of the same rows, including this numerator (0.72 +/- 0.046 also appears as normal seed treatment + soil drenching Shoot dry Weight). Internal evidence favours the saline root cells being the originals and the normal shoot cells being the misplaced copies: only the saline block carries letters; saline root values sit just below the normal root values for each route (0.44 vs 0.49, 0.29 vs 0.31, 0.50 vs 0.57, 0.72 vs 0.88 g); and the normal shoot copies would put inoculated non-saline shoots far below both the normal control and the same routes under salt, contradicting the text. This is inference, not proof: no original source prints the values independently. Discussion p.9 (receipt SRC-2832bea2dc72f2f65b1d38ae) supports only the direction of the effect, stating that seed + soil drench gave the highest root/shoot dry weight, and the supplement holds only bacterial characterization tables by keyword search of its parsed text, so neither corroborates the number. Original PDF p7 Table 1 read at 300 dpi (receipt SRC-0fd0806ea6264b05fea36260), Saline conditions block, Root dry weight (g): Positive control 0.05 ± 0.007 (b); Seed treatment 0.44 ± 0.067 (c). ln(0.44/0.05)=2.175 matches the flagged lnRR. CONTRAST IDENTITY IS INFERRED: the an_contrasts row f9637011a2a98c191e2b3171 is not in the packet and the tool guard blocked a direct database read, so I matched by arithmetic. Among the 12 saline inoculated-versus-control dry-weight ratios tested (root, shoot, root+shoot sum), only this one gives 2.175 (shoot seed treatment 2.085, root+shoot seed treatment 2.102, shoot soil drenching 2.132, root+shoot soil drenching 2.165). The mapping is seed treatment 279_EXP01_ARM07 versus saline control 279_EXP01_ARM06, root-only. The packet measurements for these arms (279_M0041, 279_M0035) equal the printed cells. Basis: Methods p11 (receipt SRC-8721a705d484aade2da7117d) states roots and shoots were oven dried separately at 60 °C for 3 days to constant weight; one plant per pot after thinning; 30-day harvest. Units are g in both arms, so no unit error explains the magnitude. WHY IT IS EXTREME: the shared saline control root dry weight is very low. All four saline root contrasts on this denominator are large (root dipping 1.758, seed treatment 2.175, soil drenching 2.303, seed+soil 2.667), so this is not an isolated single-cell anomaly. Printed two-decimal rounding alone spans about 2.07 to 2.29 for this contrast (0.435/0.055 to 0.445/0.045). Root fresh-weight lnRR for the same arms is only 0.857 (2.38/1.01). Implied root dry/fresh ratio is 5.0% in the saline control versus 18.5% in this arm, 15.7 to 20.5% in the other saline inoculated arms and 9.1% in the normal control. The authors report the dry weights as printed, so this is a plausibility caveat that the source cannot resolve, and it gives no basis for a correction. RESIDUAL LIMITATIONS TO KEEP WITH THE FLAG: (1) Source duplication: Table 1 Normal-block inoculated Shoot Length, Shoot fresh Weight and Shoot dry Weight cells repeat the Saline-block Root Length, Root fresh Weight and Root dry weight cells of the same rows, so 0.44 ± 0.067 is also printed as Normal seed treatment shoot dry weight. The Saline root cells carry significance letters and the Normal inoculated cells do not, and the Normal shoot values sit far below the Normal control (0.44 versus 0.98 g shoot dry weight), so the Normal shoot block is the more likely corrupted one. This is an inference: the pages read here give no statement of which block is correct, and no erratum was searched for. The flagged contrast uses only Saline root cells and is not directly affected, but contrasts using Normal shoot cells (279_EXP01_ARM02 to ARM05, status AMBIGUOUS) must not rely on this review. (2) Replication conflict: Methods p11 says each treatment was replicated five times; Table 1 caption says n=3 and Statistical analysis p12 (receipt SRC-1346fb61d6db7872855cb338) says triplicates. This does not alter the point lnRR but affects its variance. (3) ARM06 is a shared control, so the root contrasts are dependent. (4) validate.py computes the MAD distribution by endpoint only, so this root-only value is judged against the whole DRY_BIOMASS endpoint; root-only stays separate from whole-plant/shoot per contract. I could not confirm from the packet how this row is marked for marts. Supplement: the parsed text was searched only as a hint and mentions root only in a strain-identification title, with no plant dry-weight terms; the original docx was not rendered for this review. Fruit yield is unaffected: triage P1 and P2 record it ABSENT for this 30-day pot trial, and this review did not re-examine that.

resolution: True outlier retained; no value deleted, corrected or winsorized. CONTRAST: an_contrasts row e867923c4afc04d43d1716ad, read directly: SB_vs_S, leaf scope, g/plant, arm_key_t E1.SB.BPUM.ZnO20 mean 2.78, arm_key_c E1.S mean 0.49, n 4 and 4, effect 1.7358. SOURCE: original PDF physical p.6, Table 2, LDW (g/plant) column (receipt SRC-9375d21a107cfac47ac7ea14, PNG read at 220 dpi): row 'Salinity stress + Bacillus pumilus + 20 mg L-1 ZnO-NPs' prints 2.78 +/- 1.2 bc; row '250 mM NaCl' prints 0.49 +/- 0.9 f. The record means match the printed cells and ln(2.78/0.49) reproduces the flagged 1.736, so there is no transcription, arm or unit error. Results prose on physical p.5 (receipt SRC-ebc76e410eacaafbf17148e4, PNG read) repeats 0.49 g/plant as the lowest LDW mean, under 250 mM NaCl; this may derive from the same table, so it is consistency, not independent confirmation. CORROBORATION OF SIZE, same two rows on p.6, hand arithmetic: LFW 18.43/3.19 gives lnRR about 1.754; RFW 2.17/0.41 gives about 1.666; RDW 0.21/0.08 gives about 0.965; LDW/LFW is about 0.151 treated and 0.154 NaCl. The large effect reflects a strong reported response from a very low stressed baseline. This shows internal consistency only; it cannot prove the authors' data correct. DESIGN: p.3 Section 2.2 (receipt SRC-3adaf430ee04706dd170957c) states factorial, completely randomized, four replications; p.4 Section 2.3.4 (receipt SRC-81cfbb600a67167f92813f12) states each pot is the experimental unit with three plants selected per pot, Duncan's test; n=4 pots supported. Both arms share cultivar Linda and the experiment. LIMITATIONS THAT STAY WITH THE FLAG: (1) VARIANCE OF THIS CONTRAST IS NOT CREDIBLE AS STORED. The printed +/- is unlabelled; pages 3-6 read here define no SD or SE, so USER_ASSUMED_SE applies and the record has sd_c=1.8 and var_effect 3.5599, almost entirely from the comparator ((0.9/0.49)^2 about 3.37). For four non-negative pot values with mean 0.49, the largest possible SE equals the mean (0.49) and the largest possible SD is 0.98, so 0.9 cannot be an SE at n=4 and SD 1.8 is arithmetically impossible. Read as an SD, 0.9 would be barely possible. A misprint is plausible but the true value is not established; no replacement such as 0.09 is proposed or applied, and the printed 0.9 is preserved. This also makes effect_bc=0.142 unreliable as a correction, since it is driven by the same term. Weighted use of this contrast is unsafe, and exclusion via weighted_reported_uncertainty_only_eligible or an unweighted sensitivity analysis is advised; the same concern sits in open P003 issue 11391 and V009 issue 4899 (CV=3.67), which this decision does not close. The lnRR point value does not depend on the +/-, which is why this C001 flag is retained rather than escalated. The same pattern affects other Table 2 cells (RDW 0.21 +/- 0.81, 0.27 +/- 0.80, 0.31 +/- 0.7). (2) Comparator 0.49 is shared across SB_vs_S contrasts in this study (shared_control_id recorded; dependency cluster DC-D_0783aeacf190137b). (3) Leaf-only dry mass in seedlings, not whole-plant terminal biomass; sampling day is not stated, and Section 2.2 says only that fresh leaves were collected prior to flowering. (4) Methods name leaf dry weight and precision scales but state no oven or drying procedure; the header and Methods do say dry weight. (5) The treated arm is a PGPB plus ZnO-NP combination, and Table 2 publishes no no-bacteria plus ZnO row, so the effect cannot be attributed to one component. FRUIT YIELD: this flag concerns DRY_BIOMASS only and Table 2 has no fruit-yield column, so no retained fruit-yield data are affected. Only physical pp.3-6 were read for this issue; this is not a study-wide fruit-yield absence review.

DRY_BIOMASS lnRR=1.719 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=4.7 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: Genuine large effect, supported by the original; values retained, flag kept, nothing deleted or winsorized. Contrast 16c890e907d3d6aa72819156 (SB_vs_S, DRY_BIOMASS, SHOOT, TP_FINAL_HARVEST, g/plant): T = E1.ALF_ST_M1.T4 (tv 4114, mean 1.290), C = E1.ALF_ST_M1.T1 (tv 4111, mean 0.2312). Original PDF p7 (receipt SRC-6531372cbd9895785d88ec5e, 300 dpi) Fig. 3A, sterile Alfisol, 'with mica' group: the DWS (shoot dry weight) bar for T1 sits just above 0.2 (about 0.23) and the bar for T4 (A. violaceofuscus + B. licheniformis) sits just under 1.3 (about 1.29). The y-axis 'Biomass (g-1 plant)' has ticks 0.0/0.5/1.0/1.5. The DWS legend and caption make the organ shoot and the basis dry weight. The DMRT letters (T1 'd', T4 'a') support a large difference. Independent corroboration is on original p6 (receipt SRC-366e404459284d1403c19ac4), section 3.4.1.4 Shoot dry weight: in Alfisol, dual-inoculated shoots were '5.05 and 5.62-fold' heavier than the negative and positive control in sterile conditions. The positive control is the with-mica T1 (caption: 'T1, control (negative and positive)'). Digitized ratio 1.290/0.2312 = 5.58, within 0.7% of the printed 5.62-fold, so lnRR = 1.719 matches the author-reported effect. Arm mapping (sterile, with mica, T4 vs T1), organ, unit and timepoint are correct. Methods 2.3.4 (oven-dried 48 h at 60-65 C) confirms dry basis. The outlier comes from a very small mock-inoculated control in sterile soil, not from an extraction error. ERROR_BAR_DIGITIZATION_OVER_5PCT on the error bars (small upper caps, lower half hidden inside the bar) is acceptable under author decision 8 of 2026-11-06 and does not affect the means. var_available=0 because n is not reported, which is a known limitation already recorded in n_source.

message: DRY_BIOMASS lnRR=1.843 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=5.1 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: Genuine outlier supported by the original; retain and do not delete or winsorize. Original PDF p.6, Figure 1b (tomato; y-axis 'Shoot dry weight (gr plant-1)', 0-10, ticks every 1). In the Z. eros 2 group the D bar (light green, letter c) has its top at about 5.0, with a small SD cap of about +/-0.1. In the Control group the D bar (letter a) has its top at about 0.8. The contrast means mean_t=5.012 (E1.SB2, Z. eros 2 D) and mean_c=0.794 (E1.S, Control D) match these bar heights visually. Arm mapping (strain 2 under drought vs uninoculated under drought), organ (shoot), unit (g/plant) and timepoint (single harvest after seven weeks) are all correct. lnRR=ln(5.012/0.794)=1.843 (+531%) is consistent with the figure and with the text in Section 3.1, which says Z. erostrata 2 gave the largest shoot biomass increase in tomato under both watering regimes. Dry basis confirmed in Methods 2.4 on p.4 (receipt SRC-21c49d9114ef2a3df2f80163): DW of shoots measured after drying in a forced hot-air oven at 70 C for 48 h. The caption gives means +/- standard deviation of ten replicates, while Sec 2.3 on p.4 says four replicates for all parameters. This n conflict is already recorded (n_t/n_c null, var_available=0) and does not affect the point estimate. The ERROR_BAR_DIGITIZATION_OVER_5PCT flag is allowed under author decision 8 of 2026-11-06. No source, unit, arm or extraction error was found. The large effect comes from the very small uninoculated drought control.

message: DRY_BIOMASS lnRR=1.700 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=4.6 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: Contrast 173f79d83b9a34e24228a8c1 (DRY_BIOMASS, ROOT, TP_FINAL_HARVEST, g/plant; E1.VER_ST_M0.T4 dual BL+AV vs E1.VER_ST_M0.T1 negative control, sterile Vertisol without mica). I re-rendered original PDF p7 at 360 dpi (receipt SRC-033915aad723499f96589224) and read Fig. 3C. The y-axis is 'Biomass (g-1 plant)' with ticks 0.0/0.5/1.0/1.5/2.0/2.5, the caption says 'Shoot (DWS) and root (DWR) dry weight', and the red DWR bars sit in the 'without mica' group under 'Sterile'. In the gridded crop the axis runs about 434 zoomed px per 1.0 g. The T1 DWR bar top is at about 0.076 g/plant (letter e) and the T4 DWR bar top is at about 0.415 g/plant (letter c). These match the stored means of 0.0761 and 0.4167 within the mean tolerance. Arm, organ (root), dry basis, unit and timepoint all agree with the source. The original prose on p6 (receipt SRC-366e404459284d1403c19ac4, section 3.4.1.5 Root dry weight) independently says that in Vertisol the dual-inoculated roots were 'heavier by 5.29' versus the negative control in sterile conditions, continued on p7 as '...and 8.04-fold in sterile condition'. That gives lnRR = 1.666, against 1.700 (ratio 5.48) from the figure. The roughly 3.6% gap fits the small control bar, whose mean relative bound is 0.045. Under author decision 2 of 2026-11-05 the figure value is retained. The large effect is genuine: the authors themselves report a 5.3-fold increase, so this is not a source or extraction error. The contrast is retained unchanged and the robust-outlier flag is kept; nothing is deleted or winsorized. ERROR_BAR_DIGITIZATION_OVER_5PCT on the one-sided bars is allowed under author decision 8 of 2026-11-06. var_available=0 because n is not reported.

resolution: Contrast effea479cb47cfd038889495 (E1, season 2017, SB_vs_S, Irrig60xSe40xFS vs Irrig60xSe0xFS, FRUIT_YIELD kg plant-1, T90DAT) re-checked on the original PDF p.13 render (receipt SRC-e6807cb73bfb90987ef05d16). Fig. 9 lowest panel, y-axis 'Fruit yield plant-1 (kg)' (fresh fruit yield per plant, total, 90 DAT), black bars = Season of 2017. The black Irrig60xSe0xFS bar is about 0.4 kg (stored 0.388), with an upper cap near 0.9 (stored 0.930). message: FRUIT_YIELD lnRR=2.363 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=6.2 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: Contrast efc6af7b76b7b7ca4df165c2 (E1.SB Ampelomyces sp. vs E1.S NS, greenhouse drought, tp E1.FRUIT_CUM) checked against original PDF p.9, Fig. 5b, 'Drought treatment' group, at a 200-dpi render. Fig. 5b axis labels: '-' (zero), 1,000 to 5,000. Visually the NS black bar ends about 0.34 of the 0-1,000 interval (about 340) and the hatched Ampelomyces bar ends just under 3,600 (about 3,550 to 3,600). This matches the stored mean_c=337.6 and mean_t=3586.1, so lnRR=2.363 (about 10.6x) reflects the source. Caption: '(b) Total fruit weight produced by NS plants and plants colonized with Ampelomyces sp. and P. chrysogenum. Each data represents the means of three independent replicates and each replicate represent a minimum of 5 plants'. This supports n=3 replicates. Section 2.7 states that NS plants were 'severely wilted and unhealthy with very few flowers', and that the much higher fruit number of symbiotic plants led to a 'significant increase in the total weight of fruit'. The large ratio is therefore biologically plausible and is not a digitization or arm-assignment error. Arms, timepoint and figure panel are correct. Yield scope: Fig. 5b has no y-axis title or unit, and the caption gives no denominator ('total fruit weight produced'). The contrast signature already carries unit=UNLABELLED, mass_basis/denominator/yield_scope=UNSPECIFIED, so under author decision 4 of 2026-11-06 it stays outside strict lnRR marts (A_direct_yield_unit_unresolved). It must not be pooled with the per-plant Fig. 5a or per-plot Fig. 6 yields. The bars are unlabelled and carry USER_ASSUMED_SE. ERROR_BAR_DIGITIZATION_OVER_5PCT applies (decision 8), and the variance is unavailable because of dependence. These are not grounds to reject. The outlier is genuine: retain the value and the flag, do not delete or winsorize, no source correction required.

Independent visual read of Fig. 5b: the axis is printed '-', 1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000, 5,000 with evenly spaced gridlines; the Drought NS black bar ends clearly below the 1,000 gridline, at roughly 0.3-0.4 of the 0-1,000 interval (~340-360), and the hatched Ampelomyces bar ends between 3,000 and 4,000, at roughly 3,550-3,600. That gives a ratio of about 10 (lnRR about 2.3), so the stored means match the figure within reading resolution. The NS bar has a long error bar running from near 0 to ~650, which matches the large stored sd_c relative to mean_c. The extreme ratio is supported by the original text in Section 2.7 on the same page: 'NS plants were generally severely wilted and unhealthy with very few flowers' and 'the number of fruit produced by each symbiotic plant was much higher than in NS plants, leading to significant increase in the total weight of fruit collected'. The low NS drought total is therefore a true biological result and not a digitization, identity or scale error. Retain the record unchanged with the outlier flag; do not delete or winsorize it. Existing limitations stay in place and are not waived by this decision: the Fig. 5b unit and denominator are UNSPECIFIED (no y-axis title; the caption says total per treatment group), so the contrast belongs only in the unit-unresolved mart and must not be pooled with per-plant or per-plot yield. Its flags ERROR_BAR_DIGITIZATION_OVER_5PCT and DEPENDENT_OR_UNKNOWN_ALLOCATION_VARIANCE_UNAVAILABLE also remain, and var_effect remains unavailable.
